page.text:
In any formula involving variables, we must scrupulously distinguish
between *free* variables and *bound* variables. A free variable acts as
an open slot or parameter: it can be assigned different values from its
domain, and the truth of the formula varies with the assignment. A bound
variable, by contrast, is governed by a quantifier ($\forall$ or
$\exists$); it is an internal dummy variable whose scope is restricted to
the quantified expression.
